# Game Hosting Guides

> Independent reviews and comparisons of Minecraft and game server hosting providers. We test hosts in real-world conditions and publish results as long-form written reviews and YouTube videos.

## Reviews

- [Best Minecraft Server Hosting 2026 — comparison](https://gamehostingguides.com/best-minecraft-server-hosting/): Side-by-side comparison of 9 providers with disclosed hardware specs, pricing, and datacenter locations.
- [Apex Hosting review](https://gamehostingguides.com/reviews/apex-hosting/): Polished, well-supported Minecraft host with 18 datacenter locations and one-click modpacks.
- [BisectHosting review](https://gamehostingguides.com/reviews/bisecthosting/): 2,300+ modpack library and 21 global datacenters; Budget vs Premium tier comparison.
- [CloudNord review](https://gamehostingguides.com/reviews/cloudnord/): EU-native hosting with publicly disclosed Ryzen 7 7700 / i9-11900K hardware.
- [Hostinger review](https://gamehostingguides.com/reviews/hostinger/): VPS-based Minecraft hosting with AMD EPYC and KVM virtualization.
- [MCProHosting review](https://gamehostingguides.com/reviews/mcprohosting/): Legacy creator-partnered host, now operating under Apex Hosting after Nitrado acquisition.
- [Nodecraft review](https://gamehostingguides.com/reviews/nodecraft/): Polished NodePanel with one-click swap between 59+ games on the same server.
- [Server.pro review](https://gamehostingguides.com/reviews/server-pro/): Genuinely free tier with a real paid upgrade path.
- [ServerPrism review](https://gamehostingguides.com/reviews/serverprism/): Single plan splittable across multiple game servers, proxies, databases, and bots.
- [Shockbyte review](https://gamehostingguides.com/reviews/shockbyte/): Budget Minecraft hosting with global node coverage including Sydney and Singapore.

## Guides

- [How much RAM does a Minecraft server need?](https://gamehostingguides.com/guides/minecraft-server-ram/): Vanilla 1-5 players needs 2 GB; a plugin server wants 4 GB; a 100-mod pack wants 6-8 GB; 200+ mod packs want 10-12 GB. CPU clock matters more than RAM for TPS.
- [Why is my Minecraft server lagging?](https://gamehostingguides.com/guides/why-is-my-minecraft-server-lagging/): TPS below 20 = server-side lag (CPU, view-distance, entities, a bad plugin, or GC), not network. Diagnose with /tps or Spark; more RAM rarely fixes low TPS.
- [Minecraft server backups](https://gamehostingguides.com/guides/minecraft-server-backups/): Retention matters more than frequency; keep at least one off-site copy; back up the whole server directory (not just the world); and test a restore before you need it.
- [Best cheap Minecraft hosting under $5/mo](https://gamehostingguides.com/guides/best-cheap-minecraft-server-hosting/): Curated sub-$5 picks with disclosed CPUs and real RAM; the honest entry point is ~$2.50-$4/mo for 1-2 GB.
- [Best Minecraft hosting for modpacks](https://gamehostingguides.com/guides/best-minecraft-hosting-for-modpacks/): Modpacks need 6-12 GB, high single-thread CPU clock, and broad modloader support; undersizing on RAM or CPU causes OOM crashes and lag.
- [Java vs Bedrock Minecraft servers](https://gamehostingguides.com/guides/java-vs-bedrock-minecraft-servers/): Java has mods/plugins and is single-thread CPU-bound; Bedrock is cross-platform and lighter. Your platform and modding needs decide, not raw performance.
- [Does datacenter location matter?](https://gamehostingguides.com/guides/minecraft-server-datacenter-location/): Yes — aim for under ~80 ms ping from your typical player; a great CPU in the wrong region still feels laggy because latency is set by distance.
- [Apex Hosting vs Shockbyte](https://gamehostingguides.com/guides/apex-hosting-vs-shockbyte/): Head-to-head on price, disclosed hardware, panel, and support to pick between two of the most popular budget Minecraft hosts.
